summary: Iteration 3: validated new Series/Sequel feature and Welcome Email trigger on register. Backend (pytest, 4/4 PASS): list endpoint exposes serie_volume+parent_titolo, POST /books with valid parent inherits characters+contesto_serie+serie_volume=2, invalid parent -> 404, register triggers async welcome email (email logged in backend.err.log with expected Resend testing-mode delivery failure for non-owner recipient). Frontend (all UI flows PASS): dashboard shows Vol.2 badge only on sequel book, parent book page shows 'Scrivi il seguito' button, click navigates to /crea?sequel=<id> with sequel-banner, overline 'Nuovo volume · Vol. 2', prefilled genre/tone/length/pov and inherited characters (Elio Marchetti + Nina), remove-sequel-btn clears banner/characters and reverts overline to 'Nuova opera', in_scrittura sequel book overline shows 'Volume 2 · seguito di «Gli Orologi del Tempo Sospeso»' (serie-volume-label rendered even when status != completato). Regression: UI email/password register still lands on /dashboard with '15 crediti omaggio' welcome toast. No AI generation calls were performed - seed user still at 10 credits.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:446 & :537 fire-and-forget asyncio.create_task(_send_welcome_safe(...)) is not awaited nor stored - if the event loop shuts down before it completes the email send is silently dropped; the _send_welcome_safe wrapper already swallows exceptions so this is acceptable, but consider a lightweight task registry to allow graceful shutdown and observability.

server.py create_book: contesto_serie is built ONLY at creation time. If the parent later changes (edited chapters, updated riassunto), the sequel keeps the stale snapshot. Consider recomputing on generate-outline for the sequel, or documenting this as intentional to freeze context.

CreateBook.jsx line 57: inherited characters are copied stripping id and immagine, but tono/lunghezza/pov are unconditionally overwritten from parent - this silently discards any user-typed defaults if the user navigated to /crea WITHOUT sequel first, then added the sequel query param. Minor UX.

BookMeta.jsx serie-volume-label uses a leading '·' inside the span so full rendering becomes 'Fantasy · Volume 2 · seguito di ...' when genre is set, but produces ' · Volume 2 ...' (leading dot) when genre is empty. Consider conditional separator.
server.py _book_summary defaults serie_volume to 1 always - correct, but list endpoint returns raw dict (no Pydantic model) so future field additions are untyped.
